rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.
rules.interaction: Units subject to the RSO get just cause protection under the RSO (L.A.M.C. 151.09) instead; the JCO fills the gap for non-RSO units and layers on state AB 1482 just cause.

all.unavailable: single-family home or condominium owned by a non-corporate, non-trust owner who gave written notice of exemption

any.unavailable: transient hotel, licensed care facility, fraternity or sorority house, owner's roommate, qualifying cooperative, homeless or treatment nonprofit facility, HACLA or government property

rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals not regulated by the RSO (buildings newer than October 1, 1978, and single-family dwellings); tenant in unit at least six months or original lease expired
rules.exemptions: transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity/sorority houses, owner's roommate, some cooperatives, some nonprofit homeless or treatment facilities, some HACLA/government property; single-family home or condo only if not owned by a trust, corporation or LLC with a corporate member and tenant got written notice
rules.key_value: just cause required; relocation assistance for no-fault evictions
rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not end a tenancy without just cause (at-fault or no-fault reasons listed in the ordinance) and must pay relocation assistance for no-fault evictions. Applies to units not covered by the RSO once the tenant has lived there six months or the original lease expired.

rules.quoted_span: limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region
rules.conflict_note: Secondary city web page; it lists stale annual percentages (8.9% for Aug 2024 to Jul 2025) and gives no effective date for the statute, so effective_date is left null.
rules.interaction: Yields to stricter local rent control such as the LA RSO for units covered by it.

all.unavailable: single-family home or condominium owned by a non-corporate, non-trust owner who gave written notice of exemption
owner occupied the second unit for the entire tenancy

rules.exemptions: units built within the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable units; certain dormitories; two-unit property where an owner occupied the second unit for the whole tenancy; single-family homes and condos if owner is not a trust, corporation or LLC with a corporate member and tenant got written notice
rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) annual rent cap
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases are capped at 5% plus the regional change in the cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower, for covered buildings older than 15 years.
